submodules.contenido:
The **Tree of Life** is a map of ten **Sefirot** (emanations, or channels of the divine energy) connected by twenty-two paths.

It isn't a physical tree, but a diagram of how the **Infinite (Ein Sof)** creates and sustains the finite world.

It's organized in three columns: the right one (**expansion**), the left one (**restriction**) and the central one (**balance**).

The tree emerges in the south of France in the twelfth century, in the school of Rabbi Isaac the Blind.

The human soul and the soul of the universe are structured along this map.

*Human suffering comes from the imbalance of these dimensions.*

That's why, in order to understand ourselves and reach inner peace and our union with our essence, we have to understand the dimensions.

The traditional descending order is: **Keter**, **Chokhmah**, **Binah**, **Chesed**, **Gevurah**, **Tiferet**, **Netzach**, **Hod**, **Yesod** and **Malkhut**.

The first three form the plane of the intellect (**ChaBaD**: Chokhmah-Binah-Da'at); the lower seven, the plane of the emotions.

**Da'at** (knowledge) isn't an independent Sefirah, but the point where Chokhmah and Binah come together to produce action.

*In inner work, Keter can be experienced as the awareness that there's always a deeper level of growth.*

It's the only dimension where truth lives; everything else is made of transitory levels of truths.

It's considered the intermediary between the **Ein Sof** and the rest of the Sefirot: the bridge between the infinite and the manifested.

It represents the **divine will**, the first impulse toward creation.

Chokhmah is the **flash of pure inspiration**, the raw idea before it has a form.

Its name is read as koach-mah, *the potential of what is*.

Its distortion, without Binah to give it form, is scattering: brilliance without coherence.

Binah takes the flash of Chokhmah and processes it, gives it structure, detail and form.

It creates the classifications we see reality through.

Its Hebrew root has to do with **separating** and **discerning**.

It's called *the higher Mother* and *the womb of creation*, where raw wisdom becomes an understandable concept.

It's the child of Binah and Chokhmah: the knowledge born of wisdom and intelligence.

It's our perspectives, what we think we know.

*Da'at grows when good use is made of Binah.*

Chesed is **unconditional Love** and giving without limits.

*The mercy and the Love we give outward are proportional to the ones we give ourselves.*

It isn't always yes: you have to learn to say no and to lower your barriers.

We give, but sometimes you can't give everything you'd like to, because the other person isn't able to receive it.

*I give for the pleasure of giving.*

---

You have to learn to give, but not beyond what you can.

The negative of Chesed (its kelipah) is giving more than you're able to.

Gevurah is **discipline**, **restriction** and the ability to set limits.

It's the strength that lets you tell apart what the other person wants from what you want.

*We have to learn to say no.*

Not giving false hope is a form of strength.

Its negative side is excessive severity.

Tiferet is **beauty**, **compassion** and the balance between right and left.

It's the center: balance toward others and with ourselves.

*It's the reconciliation of opposites.*

The Love of Chesed has to be balanced with the severity of Gevurah.

*In it we find peace.*

**Netzach** is the ability to hold a direction in spite of the difficulties.

It means *victory*, *perseverance* or *eternity*.

Together with Hod it regulates how, and how much, the energy reaches downward.

*The real victory is recognizing our feelings.*

We shouldn't repress what we feel.

Dance, music and art are forms of expression.

*You have to feel the pain when the pain is there.*

Hod means **splendor**, but also **humility** and **acknowledgment**.

If Netzach is the impulse that pushes forward, Hod is the ability to stop, listen and accept.

*It lets us recognize our limits, admit our mistakes and learn from others.*

It's also related to language and communication.

*Humility isn't thinking less of yourself, it's seeing reality with as little distortion as possible.*

Its negative side is **self-deception**.

Yesod means **foundation**.

It's the dimension that gathers the energies of all the previous Sefirot and turns them into something able to manifest.

It represents the **bond**, the **connection** and the ability to relate to ourselves, to others and to the world.

*Our identity is built in Yesod, because this is where we integrate our ideas, emotions and experiences.*

It's also related to intimacy, trust and sexual energy.

Its negative side is **false identity**.

Malkhut is the **kingdom**, the receiver of all the higher Sefirot, identified with the **Shekhinah**.

It's the final realization of the whole process: the light that descends until it becomes world.

We're physical beings connected to divinity, and we receive the energy of all the other dimensions.

*Making matter holy is the highest virtue.*

---

*Physical evil is the most condensed form of the manifestation of evil, but rejecting the material because you believe it's bad is also a form of negativity.*

opciones: A) Too much Binah without Chokhmah.
B) Too much Chokhmah without Binah.
C) Too much Yesod without Malkhut.
ejercicios.enunciado: Someone has brilliant ideas all the time, but never manages to develop them or turn them into concrete projects. Which imbalance best describes this situation?

opciones: A) Creating new ideas spontaneously.
B) Connecting wisdom and intelligence to generate knowledge you can apply.
C) Balancing the emotions of the lower plane.
ejercicios.enunciado: According to the text, what function does Da'at fulfill?

opciones: A) Chesed.
B) Gevurah.
C) Hod.
ejercicios.enunciado: Someone helps everyone, never says no, and ends up exhausted and resentful. Which Sefirah is acting in a distorted way?

opciones: A) Punishing any mistake severely.
B) Repressing emotions in order to stay in control.
C) Setting clear limits even when they're uncomfortable.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which of the following situations best represents a healthy Gevurah?

opciones: A) They're opposing forces that have to cancel each other out.
B) They have to be balanced in order to produce a healthy expression.
C) Chesed is superior and Gevurah is a temporary correction.
ejercicios.enunciado: What is the relationship between Chesed and Gevurah according to the text?

opciones: A) Hod.
B) Netzach.
C) Malkhut.
ejercicios.enunciado: Someone recognizes that they were wrong, accepts reality and changes their behavior. Which Sefirah shows up most clearly?

opciones: A) It's the origin of every creative idea.
B) It integrates the previous energies and gets them ready to manifest.
C) It's the dimension where absolute truth lives.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which statement best reflects the role of Yesod?

opciones: A) Recognizing a mistake of your own.
B) Listening to different perspectives.
C) Denying real abilities in order to get approval.
ejercicios.enunciado: According to the text, which would be an example of false humility rather than genuine Hod?

opciones: A) That real victory means recognizing what we feel.
B) That perseverance demands eliminating the emotions.
C) That the emotions belong to Hod and nowhere else.
ejercicios.enunciado: Someone feels fear, sadness and frustration, but insists on ignoring them in order to keep going. Which teaching of Netzach are they neglecting?

opciones: A) Turning inspiration into knowledge.
B) Turning spiritual energy into manifested reality.
C) Keeping the balance between Love and discipline.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which of the following sentences best sums up the function of Malkhut?
